submission.justification: Crystal-K1 gives the best resolution (2.93% FWHM at 5 cm), but the Q1 2026 radiopurity assay measured its intrinsic background at 2.0 ± 0.2 counts/kg/day. That is 4 times the facility budget of 0.5 counts/kg/day, and the background comes from contamination inside the crystal itself, so shielding cannot remove it. K1 therefore fails the low-background constraint. Crystal-K3 (0.30 ± 0.05 counts/kg/day) and Crystal-K2 (0.10 ± 0.03) both fit within the budget. Of the two, K3 has much better resolution (about 4.5% compared with 8.1% for K2 at 5 cm). Thickness scan for K3 (% FWHM): 2 cm 5.16, 3 cm 4.65, 4 cm 4.50, 5 cm 4.47, 6 cm 4.58, 8 cm 5.17, 10 cm 6.31. The optimum is broad at 4–5 cm, and 5 cm gave the lowest value. 4 cm and 5 cm differ by less than the likely noise between simulation runs, so 5 cm sits in the middle of the plateau and matches the 2025 nominal design. Recommendation: Crystal-K3 at 5 cm. This is the best resolution available among the crystals that meet the low-background requirement.

requirements.requirement: Best possible energy resolution at 662 keV
requirements.evidence: K3 at 5 cm gives 4.47% FWHM, the best of the scanned thicknesses (2–10 cm). It is the best resolution among the crystals that meet the background budget. K1 would give 2.93% but is excluded by the background budget; K2 gives 8.09%.

requirements.requirement: Crystal must be one of the three candidates in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Crystal-K3 is listed in candidate_specs.md and available in the required sizes.

Q1 2026 HPGe assay: K3 intrinsic background 0.30 ± 0.05 counts/kg/day, within the 0.5 counts/kg/day facility budget (K1 measured 2.0, so excluded). The lead/copper shielding and radon purge are in operation.
